cases.caseName: Ex parte State ex rel. Lamon
cases.rule: Child-support installments become final judgments when due; amounts accruing before a modification petition generally are not modifiable, and a trial court cannot forgive an accrued arrearage.

cases.caseName: State Department of Human Resources ex rel. McGhee v. McGhee
cases.rule: Past-due support is a final judgment as it becomes due; when post-judgment interest is properly requested, failure to impose it is error.

cases.caseName: State Department of Human Resources ex rel. Laro v. Gray
cases.rule: DHR contempt cases involving arrears; properly requested post-judgment interest on child-support arrearages should be awarded.

cases.caseName: Ex parte St. Clair County Department of Human Resources
cases.rule: Rule 32 child-support determinations consider parental resources, not merely salary or wage income.
Joint/shared physical custody may support a deviation from the guidelines, but shared custody did not automatically require deviation under the Rule 32 framework then in effect.
For a self-employed parent, the court must consider business net income consistent with Rule 32 rather than relying only on salary or draw.
Business profits/net income can be relevant to child-support income; a parent should not benefit from failure to produce requested financial data.
A voluntary-underemployment finding calls for imputed earning capacity to be used within the child-support guidelines rather than simply choosing a support figure outside the guidelines.

cases.topic: Contempt / Rule 32 forms / ability to pay
cases.rule: Addresses voluntary underemployment, contempt for nonpayment, Rule 32 guideline-form compliance, and incarceration issues.
Addresses incarceration for civil contempt based on child-support arrears and the obligor's asserted inability to pay the purge amount.
A party seeking modification bears the burden of showing changed circumstances; Rule 32 applies once the modification threshold is met, subject to applicable presumptions and deviation rules.
Recent Jefferson County juvenile-court appeal involving a default paternity judgment, child-support order, and later contempt/arrearage proceedings; useful for default-order and enforcement research.

cases.caseName: Wilton Lee Triggs, II v. Brittany Denece Triggs
cases.rule: Recent child-support modification decision discussing material/substantial/continuing change and trial-court discretion concerning retroactivity to the filing date of a modification petition.
Reaffirms that matured child-support payments become final judgments and accrued arrears cannot simply be forgiven; cites Ex parte Lamon and related authority.
A deviation from Rule 32 requires evidence-based findings sufficient to justify the deviation; also discusses retroactive child-support issues.
